name: Tuxá
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Extinct, unclassified; only wordlists (Nimuendaju) known. No grammar/phonology describing stress located.

sources.citation: SIL Brazil archive record 16988 for Meader 1978 (metadata page)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Metadata only: 94 pp. print, 'reformatted from the original print version, but the content is identical'; subject languages include Tuxá [tud]; PDF link on sil.org is behind an automated-access block (could not be reached by automated download and direct download), copy obtained from the the Internet Archive.
No descriptive references at all (only Fabre 2005 for classification and Ethnologue for endangerment status: 'Tuxá (tud-tud) = 9 (Dormant)'); alternative names Tuxa, Rodela, Todela, Tusha, Tushá.

Secondary; both reproduce the Pompeu 1958 (14 words) and Meader 1978 (~30 words, with the stress marks) lists and name no other linguistic source; en page gives the SIL Brazil record URL for Meader 1978 and the etnolinguistica.org PDF for Pompeu 1958.

sources.citation: Durazzo, Leandro. 2017. Apontamentos sobre língua indígena no Nordeste: Os Tuxá do Submédio São Francisco. Novos Debates 3(1-2): 33-36. doi:10.48006/2358-0097-3105
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or phonology; an anthropological note on the present-day Tuxá of Rodelas, who 'dizem falar cotidianamente o Dzubukuá, sua língua ancestral' -- i.e. it concerns the Kariri language Dzubukuá being revitalised, not the extinct Tuxá isolate. Cites Durazzo 2018 (ANPOCS) 'Língua indígena no Submédio São Francisco: Tuxá, Truká e a rede procá de revitalização político-linguística do Dzubukuá'.

sources.citation: Fabre, Alain. 2005-. Diccionario etnolingüístico y guía bibliográfica de los pueblos indígenas sudamericanos: TUXÁ (2 pp., last modified 2009)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No linguistic data; classifies Tuxá as 'Lengua aislada', notes that in 1961 two elders remembered some words (Meader 1978) and that the Tuxá now speak only Portuguese; bibliography is ethnographic (Carvalho, Nasser, Silva, Dantas et al.) plus Meader 1978 and Pompeu 1958.

sources.citation: Meader, Robert E. 1978. Indios do Nordeste: Levantamento sobre os remanescentes tribais do nordeste brasileiro. Série Lingüística 8. Brasília: Summer Institute of Linguistics. (2006 reformatted SIL PDF, 60 pp; Tuxá §1.3 p. 9, wordlist §3.8 p. 30, Tuxá bibliography p. 56)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology section and no remark on stress. §3.8 (p. 30) gives 'Tuxá. Lista 1' (~30 items, informant Maria Dias dos Santos, b. Rodelas, collected by Wilbur Pickering, 1961) with a stress tick ' before the stressed syllable on each item, e.g. ka'ka 'cabeça', kaka'i 'cabelo', kašu'i 'cachorro', o'tiši 'carne', to'e 'fogo', pa'ka 'fumo', kalatu'i 'muitas', 'munduřu 'panela', ša'řola 'sol'; the ' is not explained anywhere in the book. §1.3 (p. 9): the language 'já não é falada há quase 100 anos'.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian Languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center. §30 'Tusha, isolated language' (c. p. 87-88) and comparative table 'Isolated languages'
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Entry reads: 'Tushá - originally spoken on the São Francisco River near Gloria, now in the village of Rodelas, state of Pernambuco. [Pompeu Sobrinho 1958, pp. 12-13.]' and re-tabulates a few Pompeu items (takaí, kramake:, enke:, zyerome:ke:, zyerintin, zyunkurun) with vowel-length colons in place of Pompeu's circumflexes.

sources.citation: Pompeu Sobrinho, Th. 1958. Línguas Tapuias desconhecidas do Nordeste: Alguns vocabulários inéditos. Boletim de Antropologia (Universidade do Ceará) 2(1): 3-19. Tuxá = 'Vocabulário nº 3', pp. 12-13 (14 words collected by Carlos Estêvão de Oliveira, Museu Goeldi, before 1940, from Antônio Likaro and Cordorina, 'caboclos da Tribo Tushá, Rodelas')
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No statement on stress placement; only a transcription convention (p. 14): 'adotamos a ortografia e os sinais diacríticos usados pelo Dr. Carlos Estêvam, isto é, as convenções seguintes: Acento agudo para a tônica; [macron] sílaba longa; / sinal indicando palavra sincopada; Sh igual a x'. The 14 Tuxá items carry those marks: Enkê 'sol', Jerõmêkê 'lua', Eisrêmêkê 'céu', Jerintin 'terra', Kaleshí 'Rio S. Francisco', Junkurun 'homem', Lãkãtí 'mulher', Jití 'menino', Kaití 'menina', Tixí 'cabelo', Takaí 'dente', Kramakê 'orelha', Tôrú 'cachimbo', Tishiriú 'teiú'.

sources.citation: Durazzo, Leandro. 2018. Língua indígena no Submédio São Francisco: Tuxá, Truká e a rede procá de revitalização político-linguística do Dzubukuá. Anais do 42º Encontro Anual da ANPOCS, Caxambu
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Documents what today's Tuxá call their language; it is Dzubukuá (Kariri, dzub1241), so it cannot supply a stress statement for the Tuxá isolate but is needed to keep the two identities apart in the catalog.

sources.citation: Jolkesky, Marcelo P. V. 2016. Estudo arqueo-ecolinguístico das terras tropicais sul-americanas. Doctoral dissertation, Universidade de Brasília
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Comparative treatment of the NE Brazilian isolates; may re-tabulate the Tuxá items and comment on their reliability; no stress statement expected. UnB repository could not be reached by automated download at download time.

sources.citation: Original 1961 SIL/Museu Nacional survey field notes and recordings for Tuxá (Wilbur Pickering, Rodelas/Juazeiro; 'meia hora' of Tuxá dances recorded and 'arquivada no Museu Nacional', Meader 1978 p. 9)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only stress-marked Tuxá data ever elicited; the field notes could show how Pickering heard the accent and whether the double-marked forms are secondary stress. Survival after the 2018 Museu Nacional fire unknown.

sources.note: Glottolog's top-ranked reference; predates the publication of the Tuxá vocabulary, so it can only supersede nothing, but should be checked to close the Glottolog list.

sources.citation: Carlos Estêvão de Oliveira, manuscript vocabularies from the remnant groups of Pernambuco and Alagoas (incl. 'Tushá, Rodelas'), entrusted to Pompeu Sobrinho in 1940; Oliveira, C. E. de. 1931. mss. e informações. Revista do Museu Paulista 17
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Primary record behind Pompeu's 14-word list, with Estêvão's own diacritics ('acento agudo para a tônica'); Museu Goeldi/Museu Paulista holdings; would confirm stress marks on the earliest attestation.

sources.citation: Dantas, Sampaio & Carvalho 1998 (História dos Índios no Brasil, 431-456); Nasser 1975 'Sociedade Tuxá' (MA, UFBa); Nasser & de Souza 1988; Carvalho 1982; Silva 1997 'Tuxá: Índios do nordeste' (Annablume)
